message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and boots from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS.  
The example uses the `gcloud` command‑line tool (the most common way to create instances), but I also include the equivalent **REST API** payload so you can hit the Compute Engine API directly if you prefer.

> **Prerequisites**  
> * You must have a Google Cloud project with **billing enabled**.  
> * The **Compute Engine API** and the **Compute Engine GPU API** must be enabled.  
> * You need a **GPU quota** for the zone you choose (e.g., `nvidia-a6000`).  
> * The `gcloud` CLI must be installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`).  

---

## 1. Using `gcloud`

```bash
# Variables – change as needed
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM (adjust as required)
GPU_COUNT=1
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \
  --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: your init script
  --tags=http-server,https-server \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. Format: `type=<GPU_TYPE>,count=<GPU_COUNT>` |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Selects Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the root disk. |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for better performance. |
| `--tags` | Opens ports 80/443 if you want a web server. |
| `--scopes` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access (adjust as needed). |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, just bump `GPU_COUNT`.  
> **Tip:** For a **pre‑emptible** instance, add `--preemptible`.

---

## 2. Using the REST API

If you want to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), use the following JSON payload. Replace the placeholder values with your own.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to POST this payload

```bash
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **Note:** The `acceleratorType` URL must match the zone and GPU type.  
> **Note:** Ensure you have the **Compute Engine API** and **GPU API** enabled, and that your service account has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu --zone=us-central1-a
```

You should see:

* `guestAccelerators` listing the RTX A6000.  
* `status: RUNNING`.  
* `networkInterfaces` with an external IP (unless you omitted it).  

---

## 4. Optional: Install NVIDIA drivers automatically

If you want the GPU drivers to be installed automatically, add a startup script that runs `sudo ubuntu-drivers autoinstall` or use the `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` flag. Example `startup.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
apt-get update
apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

---

### Recap

| Tool | Command | What it does |
|------|---------|--------------|
| `gcloud compute instances create` | Creates the instance with GPU, OS, disk, network, tags, scopes. |
| REST API POST | Same as above but via HTTP. |

Pick whichever method fits your workflow. Happy GPU computing!
